lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-type SOLD = A$40 (Gowans 373824, black 1950s 99K type). 40 / 1.22 = 32.8, round down to A$30 hammer (A$36.60 all-in). Flip: likely resale = middle of close SOLD results, A$80 hammer, resold through a local auction at an assumed 15% seller commission (A$12), outbound postage A$0 (pickup sale, a cased machine is too heavy to post profitably) = A$68 net. 68 / 2.44 = 27.9, round down to A$25. Flip margin is thin, so KEEP only, for someone who wants a usable machine.
lots.confidence_reason: Several Tasmanian SOLD results opened with photos checked, but the model plate is not read (99K vs 201K unconfirmed) and the machine is untested, so not High.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the eBay 156721669145 'sold AU$345' and 'asking AU$390' claims: snippet only, eBay is closed to us, and the same item number was claimed as both sold and live, which cannot both be right; it is also a bentwood-lid 201K with attachments, a different spec. Dropped Gowans Featherweight 221K/222K lots 385929 (A$420), 401779 (A$460), 426252 (A$490): verified in the API but a different, much more collectable model, not comparable. LiveAuctioneers and other general searches not repeated (WebSearch budget used up this turn).
lots.key_photo_findings: Gold SINGER arm decal, stitch-length lever plate and round gold medallion on the pillar, covered handwheel with rear-mounted motor and cord wound round the head. Serial plate on the bed reads EMO 2171 with a chrome pin in the gap (likely EM plus six digits, partly hidden). Model plate not visible. Teak-look wooden base; grey houndstooth case with tan band and brass latches. No foot controller seen in the photos.
lots.condition: Paint and decals look clean and bright with little wear; cord is old rubber-sheathed and may be perished; untested per catalogue; case sound with light scuffs. Foot pedal, key and accessories not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the foot controller included, and does the case lock have a key? Can you read the model number (99K or 201K) on the plate under the bed or on the pillar, and is the wiring perished or cracked?

lots.what_it_is: Large two-tier timber canteen (lid tray plus drawer, green baize) holding about 100 to 130 pieces of matching flatware with dense all-over floral repousse-style handles, knives with plain stainless-looking blades, plus a pierced server. Catalogue title (truncated) names National Silver, an American plate maker, so most likely silver plate; no mark is readable in the photos, so plate versus sterling and the pattern are unconfirmed. The pattern looks like a copy of the Kirk/Stieff Repousse style, not National Silver's Rose and Leaf.
